The user wants details of two exhibitions: "Wonder of Nature" at Louvre Museum and "Age of Reptiles" at British Museum. They want details including child and adult admission fees.

We have a function `museum_exhibition_detail` that can provide details of a particular exhibition in a museum, including cost per visit for different age groups. We need to call this function twice: once for each exhibition.

We need to pass the exhibition name, museum name, and visitor type (child or adult). The default is adult if not specified. But we need both child and adult costs. So we should call the function twice for each exhibition: one with visitor_type="child", one with visitor_type="adult". Or maybe we can pass an array? The function signature says visitor_type?: "child" | "adult"[], so we can pass an array of types. That might return details for both. But I'm not sure if the function supports returning multiple types. It says "including the cost per visit for different age groups." So likely it returns details for all age groups. So we can just call with no visitor_type to get all. But the function signature says visitor_type defaults to ['adult']. So if we don't specify, we only get adult. So we need to specify both child and adult. We can pass ["child","adult"].

Thus we will call the function twice: one for Louvre, one for British Museum. For each call, we pass exhibition_name, museum_name, visitor_type=["child","adult"]. Then we will get details. Then we will format the answer.
